title: Anchors and choosing your reaction
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: How do you choose to react when the old trigger fires?
I said that a negative anchor might be a father, a coach or a teacher who created a negative moment, so that now you lack confidence in a subject. There are also positive anchors.
I said that as adults we regulate those moments: in NLP one of the main ideas is that you decide for yourself how you react to the events in your life.
A student said that in golf and any sport the most important thing is preparation, especially in golf where you cannot rely on teammates.
I said that you have to allow yourself to make adjustments, and not second-guess yourself, but be intuitive.
Another said that in running, by the end of the third mile you want to stop, which is a good picture for thinking about business and sport.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write how you would like to react.
Write the preparation that makes it easier.
Write your plan for the last mile.

check.q: What did I say you decide in NLP?
What did a student say is most important in a sport?
What did I say about adjustments?

recap: Choose your reaction. Prepare. Allow the adjustment.
